As I sat on the worn wooden bench, the creaking of the old wooden slats echoed through the deserted alley like the whispers of a thousand forgotten memories. The air was alive with the sweet scent of blooming jasmine, and the distant hum of city life hummed a soothing melody that seemed to lull the world into a state of slumber.

But I wasn't here to sleep. I was on a mission. A mission to uncover the truth about the small, intricately carved wooden box that lay on the bench before me. It was a plain, unassuming thing – stained brown and adorned with a delicate silver clasp – but there was something about it that drew me in, like a moth to a flame.

As I picked up the box, the silver clasp sprang open with a soft click, releasing a puff of perfumed cigarette smoke into the air. I blinked, momentarily startled, and then my eyes adjusted to the dim light, revealing a small, yellowed piece of paper folded into a neat square inside the box.

The paper was old – yellowed with age, and creased into sharp, geometric folds – and at first, I thought it was just a piece of notebook paper with some careless scribbles on it. But as I turned it over, my heart skipped a beat. Recording the temperature reading at the corner of 5th Ave. @ 10:45 AM, 21°C

What did it mean? What connection could this have to the mysterious box? And what significance could a single temperature reading have on this otherwise ordinary-looking piece of paper? The more I pondered these questions, the more my curiosity grew, and I found myself getting caught up in a whirlpool of theories and possibilities.

Perhaps it was a note from someone who had been a detective, lost as he navigated the streets of the city, searching for something vital but ultimately lying in plain sight. Or maybe it was some lost city secretary's daily record, and the scribbled note meant little more than a service station or a comedy club's show schedule guideline.

I pressed the paper between my fingers, half-answering the what-ifs etched into the hollow canyons of my thoughts as civilization detoxified.
